Summary (auto-generated - rough):
Argentum is evaluating Redwood for latency-sensitive clinical NLP features (note extraction, summarization for EHR). Primary goals: p95 latency targets for 256-512 token responses, concurrency up to 800-1,000 active streams, streaming support, and token/sec throughput for batch offline workloads. Considering Hosted for quick launch vs Dedicated/Private for data residency and SOC2/KMS requirements. Next steps: pricing, SOC2/KMS docs, benchmark run with sample prompt set.

Topics:
- p95 targets and SLOs
- concurrency and streaming
- token/sec throughput / batching
- Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick intros on our side? i'm samir, AE, and lena is our se who will dive into perf stuff
[00:07] Maya: hi Samir, Maya here, head of ML at Argentum, we run clinical nlp pipelines, super short timelines for this call
[00:12] Carlos: Carlos, infra, i'll be the person running the benchmarks and looking at networking
[00:15] Diane: Diane, CTO - i'm mostly here for compliance and high-level constraints
[00:20] Lena: thanks, quick agenda: p95 SLOs, concurrency, streaming behavior and token/sec benchmarking, and map those to Hosted/Dedicated/Private options
[00:30] Samir: can you outline current stack and the worst case SLA you're chasing?
[00:36] Maya: sure, we're on k8s in GCP, using - um - a mix of commercial models today via public APIs, latency has been a pain. Goal is p95 < 250ms for 256 tokens, and p95 < 400ms for 512 tokens. Concurrency wise, initial is 300-500 but we need to design for bursts to 1k. Streaming is required for UX.
[00:55] Lena: okay that's helpful. when you say streaming, do you need server-sent chunks for partial tokens or full message streaming?
[01:02] Maya: SSE-like partial tokens so clients can render progressively, yes.
[01:08] Lena: good. for p95 numbers, do you have a regional requirement? where's your traffic?
[01:13] Carlos: mostly US east, some EU for clinics in London, data residency is a later ask but not immediate. We do need SOC2 and KMS for key management if we go Private.
[01:25] Samir: great, on hosting modes: Hosted (our API) is fastest to prod, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput, Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict data residency and KMS. for your latencies, Dedicated usually gives the most predictable p95 because you get isolated pools and can tune kernels.
[01:45] Maya: hmm, cost tradeoffs? we have budget constraints but if latency is critical we can commit.
[01:50] Lena: quick note: we have batching and KV caching to reduce per-token cost, but batching can increase tail latency if you over-batch; we tune batch windows to keep p95 low. also our runtime selects quantization and kernels per model to optimize latency.
[02:05] Carlos: can we run local benchmarks? we want to replicate with our prompt set.
[02:09] Samir: absolutely, we typically run a benchmark job with the customer's prompt set. Lena will run a baseline on hosted and then on Dedicated infra for a like-for-like comparison.
[02:18] Lena: question on targets: the 250ms p95 for 256 tokens, is that including network hops to client?
[02:24] Maya: they'd like perceived latency to be under 300ms including client, but server-side target should be 250ms p95.
[02:30] Lena: ok noted. for throughput: are you also doing batch embeddings / offline token/sec requirements?
[02:36] Maya: yes, offline jobs generate embeddings and summaries across terabytes of notes; we need throughput numbers - tokens/sec for batch. Current jobs do about 200M tokens/day during nightly runs. We want a config that can do 1M tokens/hour ideally.
[02:50] Carlos: and concurrency pattern is mix of streaming small requests and larger batch jobs at night. we need isolation so batches don't steal concurrency.
[02:58] Samir: that's a classic batch vs burst problem. Dedicated lets you reserve pools for online low-latency traffic and separate nodes for batch. hosted can do it but may have noisy neighbors unless you opt for dedicated capacity.
[03:12] Lena: technical detail: for streaming we keep the token generation pipeline low-latency by using continuous batching and KV cache so repeated prefixes are cheap. note sometimes transcripts say K-V cash which is wrong but -- uh -- it's K-V cache, sorry.
[03:26] Maya: about quantization and model variants: we need to know if accuracy/regression risk is measured when using int8 quant. we can't degrade clinical extraction.
[03:33] Lena: totally. we recommend A/B testing with your eval set. Redwood Optimize gives quantization profiles and quality monitoring to flag regressions. We'll include recommended thresholds.
[03:44] Carlos: networking: what about VPC peering and private egress? we might want Private to keep PHI inside our VPC with customer-managed KMS.
[03:52] Samir: Private supports customer VPC and on-prem; KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs are available for enterprise packs. We'll share SOC2 and KMS integration docs.
[04:00] Diane: what about SLA and failover? we need graceful degradation - if Dedicated pool is saturated can you fallback to a lower-tier model?
[04:07] Lena: yes, smart routing supports fallbacks by policy to compatible model variants or other regions. you can configure canary or automatic fallback.
[04:14] Maya: latency benchmarking specifics: what does your 95th look like across sequence lengths and concurrency?
[04:20] Lena: typical numbers vary by model and hardware. example: on A100-style nodes with 16-bit kernels, for a 512-token generate, p95 could be ~200-300ms at low conc, but at 500 concurrent streams it climbs. we instrument per-token time and report tokens/sec and tail latencies. we'll run tests at conc points: 50, 200, 500, 1k and report p50/p95/p99.
[04:40] Samir: also streaming reduces perceived latency because first token is returned quickly; we can measure time-to-first-token separately from total response time.
[04:47] Carlos: can you simulate our prompt distribution? we have many short prompts (avg 80 tokens) and some long (1k+).
[04:53] Lena: yes please send sample prompt set; we'll run mixed workloads. please include token histograms.
[04:59] Maya: about cost, do you have estimates tokens/sec to $/hour?
[05:03] Samir: rough back-of-envelope we can give cost per million tokens on hosted; Dedicated is a fixed commit with lower per-token if you hit utilization. We'll send detailed pricing in doc.
[05:12] Diane: security: we need audit logs and RBAC for model access, and SSO (SAML).
[05:18] Lena: we support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and detailed request tracing in the console. We'll include screenshots in the doc.
[05:25] Carlos: about benchmarks, can you also run token/sec for batch quantized models? we might use int8 for batch to save cost.
[05:31] Lena: yes, test matrix will include full-precision and quantized variants, plus batch vs streaming. we'll report tokens/sec, p95 latency, and cost per token estimates.
[05:40] Maya: for streaming, do you support partial token delta or only chunked sentences?
[05:45] Lena: streaming is token-chunked; SDKs support partial events with latency under 50ms for TTF (time-to-first token) in many configs, but depends on network and client.
[05:53] Samir: quick note - sometimes our docs say 'KV cash' in older transcripts, ignore that, it's cache.
[05:58] Carlos: ok, timeline: we'd like a bench next week and decision in 3-4 weeks, possible pilot after that.
[06:05] Samir: action items recap: i'll send pricing and SOC2/KMS docs; lena will coordinate benchmarks; maya to send prompt set. any other blockers?
[06:12] Maya: none, just one ask - can you include a dedicated hosting diagram showing reserved pools and fallback?
[06:18] Lena: yes we'll include a diagram and a sample cluster config with autoscale and reserved capacity.
[06:24] Diane: please include a note on compliance and data retention policies.
[06:28] Samir: will do. thanks everyone. end of call.
